h: Rav Yosef's Humility and "How Many Yosefs": Lowliness Born of Greatness

p: Rav Yosef, on the day of Atzeres,
how many Yosefs are there in the marketplace!"
And in the Gemara at the end of Sotah
the greatness of his stature in Torah,
"Do not teach 'humility,' for there is I"?
For one who is truly humble
is lowly in his own estimation,
and in his eyes he is inferior
a man of stature than he;
and if not, it is said,
"Every haughty heart is an abomination to Hashem."
And again, if Rav Yosef was
truly humble and lowly of spirit
how could he say of himself
and at the very pinnacle of greatness
behold, regarding Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him,
it is likewise said of him,
"And the man Moshe was very humble,
more than any man," and so on;
and according to its plain meaning,
he was lowly in his own eyes,
to the point that every person
Did he not know in his soul
that he stood on the highest level,
at the very pinnacle of the human species?
what Hashem will command concerning you."
And indeed, regarding Rav Yosef too,
exactly as they were given at Sinai.
in the episode of Rabbi Elazar the son of Rabbi Shimon,
not that he was ugly in his appearance,
in his disgraceful deeds and thoughts —
"Go to the Craftsman Who made me."
that this was Eliyahu, remembered for good,
who appeared to him in such a guise
that from this nothing at all can be determined,
that even a man who is ugly,
with deficiencies to the utmost degree,
that Hashem Yisbarach implanted this in him
so that this should be his task
"Go to the Craftsman Who made me":
than a man who was created
מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר עַל מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
what is said of Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him,
that he was very humble, more than any man,
even though he knew in his soul
the greatness of his stature and his level in holiness;
even though he knew in his soul
that he was at the stature and level of "Sinai."
For precisely this is what requires it:
because the root of their birth
was in lofty virtues and levels,
it was necessary, in proportion to this,
very great, in keeping with their stature.
Therefore they were humble and lowly
in their own eyes, greatly and truly,
And this is what Rav Yosef meant:
how many Yosefs are there in the marketplace" —
that he was lofty in his stature and level,
but rather in line with what they said
and in line with what is known,
that from the time of Matan Torah onward
the souls of Yisrael were set apart
in a treasury of their own;
and this is the meaning of
"until the souls in the Guf are depleted."
In truth, even before Matan Torah
such as the holy Avos and the like;
and from Avraham Avinu, peace be upon him,
began the two thousand years of Torah,
as our Sages, of blessed memory, said
"The Holy One, blessed be He, provided him
his two kidneys like two teachers,
and they would well forth and teach him
the souls of Yisrael were singled out
to be a treasured nation among all the peoples,
not by virtue of their deeds.
And this is what Rav Yosef said:
אִי לָאו הַאי יוֹמָא דְּקָא גָּרַם
"If not for this day which brought it about" —
the lofty souls were singled out
"how many Yosefs are there in the marketplace"
who are on a level like mine,

paragraphs.text: Pesachim 68b — "Rav Yosef, on the day of Atzeres, would say: Prepare for me a choice third-grown calf. He said: Were it not for this day that brought it about, how many Yosefs are there in the marketplace!"

paragraphs.text: Sotah 49b — "When Rebbi died, humility and fear of sin ceased. Rav Yosef said to the reciter: Do not teach 'humility,' for there is I. Rav Nachman said to the reciter: Do not teach 'fear of sin,' for there is I." Rashi: for I am humble.

paragraphs.text: Berachos 64a — "Rav Yosef was 'Sinai' and Rabbah 'an uprooter of mountains.' The hour required them. They sent there: 'Sinai' and 'an uprooter of mountains' — which takes precedence? They sent back: Sinai takes precedence, for all need the owner of the wheat. Even so, Rav Yosef did not accept, for the astrologers had told him: You will reign two years."

paragraphs.text: Taanis 20a — "A person should always be soft like a reed and not hard like a cedar. Once Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon was coming from Migdal Gedor, from the house of his teacher, riding on a donkey along the riverbank, and he was greatly joyful, and his mind was proud, because he had learned much Torah."

paragraphs.text: Avodah Zarah 5a — "Rabbi Yosi said: Ben David will not come until all the souls in the Guf are used up, as it says, 'For the spirit before Me wraps itself, and the souls I have made' (Yeshayahu 57:16)."

paragraphs.text: Tosafos, Avodah Zarah 5a (s.v. ein ben David) — "'The son of David will not come until all the souls in the guf are finished.' And if you ask: they could be finished through the gentiles who give birth — Rabbi Elchanan says that the souls of Israel and of the gentiles are not in one guf."
